title: Code Grammar artifact
description: Shape authority for *.code-grammar.json artifacts, bootstrapped from what the parser consumes today (src/io/code_parser.cpp:parse_with_grammar) and intended to become the contract the generator, parser and validator all model. A checker must never manufacture the authority it verifies: a missing source is reported, never reverse-engineered from the artifact.

lexicon.description: Declared lexical layer compiled from the EBNF's @lex/@profile sections; the runtime scanner is src/util/lexicon.cpp. At each byte position the profile's kept classes are tried in keep order (keep order is match priority); the first class matching at that position wins and the match is consumed wholesale. action skip discards the match, text records it (lowercased under the profile), atom/punct record it verbatim; bytes matched by no kept class are separators. Absent when the EBNF declares no @lex section.

authored_not_generated.note: Present in every shipped artifact, emitted by no checked-in generator invocation, and consumed by no code in src/, tools/ or data/. Recorded here so the finding is preserved rather than normalised away by a regeneration check.

source_expected_semantics: false = absence is a historical repository condition (UNVERIFIED, not a failure). true = Advisor has authored the source, so absence is damage or drift and must fail. Flipping a language to true is a deliberate authority act, performed when Advisor authors its grammar.

verification_algebra.VERIFIED: shape valid, source present, regeneration matches the generated subset
verification_algebra.INVALID: schema violation, or a declared source is missing, or regeneration disagrees
verification_algebra.UNVERIFIED: no canonical source available; absence of proof is representable and is neither PASS nor FAIL
